sentence: The new policy has opened a can of worms for the department
explanation: 'Open a can of worms' significa crear problemas inesperados. Presente perfecto para un resultado reciente.

sentence: If she had not jumped on the bandwagon the project would have failed
hint: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle
explanation: 'Jump on the bandwagon' significa sumarse a una tendencia popular. Tercer condicional para un pasado irreal.

sentence: The CEO has been pulling strings behind the scenes for months
explanation: 'Pull strings' significa usar influencias en secreto. 'Behind the scenes' significa en privado.

sentence: We need to get to the bottom of this financial discrepancy
explanation: 'Get to the bottom of' significa descubrir la causa real. 'Need to' + forma base del verbo.

sentence: I wish they would stop beating a dead horse about the old strategy
hint: Wish + would + base form for complaints
explanation: 'Beat a dead horse' significa perder el tiempo en un asunto ya resuelto. 'Wish + would' para quejas.

sentence: The startup managed to weather the storm during the economic crisis
explanation: 'Weather the storm' significa superar un período difícil. 'Managed to' + forma base del verbo.

sentence: Had he not cut corners the product would have been safer
hint: Inverted third conditional: Had + subject + not + past participle
explanation: 'Cut corners' significa hacer algo de forma barata o descuidada. El condicional invertido omite 'if'.

sentence: She was barking up the wrong tree by blaming the intern
explanation: 'Bark up the wrong tree' significa seguir un enfoque equivocado. 'By' + gerundio explica cómo.

sentence: The team has been bending over backwards to meet the deadline
hint: Present perfect continuous for ongoing effort
explanation: 'Bend over backwards' significa esforzarse al máximo. Presente perfecto continuo para indicar duración.

sentence: They would rather not rock the boat before the merger is complete
explanation: 'Rock the boat' significa causar problemas. 'Would rather not' expresa preferencia por evitar algo.

sentence: We will cross that bridge when we come to it
explanation: 'Cross that bridge when we come to it' significa ocuparse de un problema solo cuando realmente ocurre.

sentence: After three failed attempts she decided to throw in the towel
hint: Time expression + subject + verb + infinitive + idiom
explanation: 'Throw in the towel' significa rendirse o admitir la derrota.

sentence: The manager should have read the writing on the wall
explanation: 'Read the writing on the wall' significa reconocer señales claras de que algo malo está por suceder.

sentence: The negotiations collapsed and we had to go back to square one
hint: Clause + and + subject + had to + idiom
explanation: 'Go back to square one' significa volver a empezar desde el principio después de un contratiempo.

sentence: Regular exercise helps keep stress at bay
explanation: 'Keep something at bay' significa evitar que algo te afecte o se acerque a ti.

sentence: She could not help because she had a lot on her plate
explanation: 'Have a lot on your plate' significa tener muchas responsabilidades a la vez.

sentence: The manager decided to turn a blind eye to the mistake
hint: Subject + decided to + idiom + to + object
explanation: 'Turn a blind eye' significa ignorar algo deliberadamente.

sentence: You should never burn bridges with former colleagues
explanation: 'Burn bridges' significa romper relaciones de forma irreparable.

sentence: Managers must nip small problems in the bud
explanation: 'Nip something in the bud' significa cortar un problema de raíz antes de que crezca.

sentence: The accountant keeps tabs on every expense
explanation: 'Keep tabs on' significa vigilar o hacer seguimiento de algo de cerca.
